name: spec
description: Spec pipeline v7 — a small code program run by a trusted engineer, verified by executed evidence. Lifecycle: /spec:genesis (greenfield) → roadmap briefs → /spec:mocks → /spec:plan → /spec:run (build, then review, each driver-stepped with one fresh-context reviewer and a derived verdict) → /spec:release; plus /spec:status, /spec:doctor, /spec:enforce, /spec:fix. Changelog (last 3): 7.300.0 — core § Doctrine Authoring now names the three kinds of prose pin (references, retired phrases, protocol tokens) and states that a pin on the wording of a rule is not a test; wording is read by review. 7.299.0 — red-check.js now applies the host's declared testCountPattern to each run's output and raises the hard finding vacuous-green when a sanctioned-green file executed no test (one warning when the pattern is undeclared); memory-sweep.js matches changed paths without an extension list so non-JS hosts surface agent memory for disposal, and an uncommitted note ages from its file mtime. 7.298.0 — workspace-scan.js now emits one {root, stack, manifest} row per (directory, stack) pair instead of the first manifest only, so a polyglot root (package.json beside pyproject.toml, go.mod, Cargo.toml …) gets /spec:enforce cells for every stack. Manifests of one stack still collapse to one row; single-stack output is unchanged. Re-run /spec:enforce on polyglot hosts to pick up the missing stacks.
